activeForm: json-rt: a cl-ppcre char class is a loop over per-item closures; a 256-bit table is -10 % (filed, under the bar)
description:
json-rt (perf round 45, s514c member 2 candidate, FILED -- under the 15 % bar): cl-ppcre's vendored `convert-char-class-to-test-function` (cl/vendor/cl-ppcre/convert.lisp:84) turns a char class into a LOOP over per-item closures (`thereis (funcall test-function char)`), and `*optimize-char-classes*` is NIL, so every char of a JSON::PP string scanned by `s/([\x22\x5c\n\r\t\f\b])/.../g` / `s/([\x00-\x08\x0b\x0e-\x1f])/.../eg` walks that list.  Profile (s514c, N=100): `(lambda (char) :in convert-char-class-to-test-function)` 9.9 % self / 14.7 % cum, the scanner lambda in create-scanner-aux 7.0 % self / 20 % cum.

Hand-replaced A/B (scratch/s514c/prof/leverC.lisp in worktree agent-ab5b9d32441dad215): a class whose items are all chars/ranges below 256 and not case-insensitive becomes ONE 256-bit sbit lookup (codes >= 256: false, inverted: true): json-rt whole run 2.06-2.09 -> 1.91-1.93 s (-7.5 % wall, ~-10 % of the bench's exec metric), output identical.  The char-class frame leaves the profile; the scanner's per-position loop (12.5 % cum) remains -- a pattern that STARTS with a char class has no start-string skip, so the matcher is called at every position.

Not shipped: under 15 %.  Where it would go: NOT in cl-ppcre (DECIDED: rewrites live in PCL's scanner wrapper) -- a parse-tree rewrite in %pcl-build-scanner (a `(:char-class ...)` of plain chars/ranges -> a resolver-backed `(:property key)` whose resolver returns the bitmap test; /i or inline (?i) anywhere = decline), combined with a leading-char-class skip loop in the same wrapper to clear the bar.
